corrections.issue: Mixes speakers: the AI narrative shift (from all positive to winners and losers, software selloff) is Alan Dunne's observation; Mark only defines narrative as storytelling used when risk is not countable.
corrections.fix: Mark: a narrative is storytelling used where risk is not countable (uncertainty), so hard-to-measure themes like AI are priced on stories.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker for 'not yet reached': Alan Dunne says fiscal dominance is a risk but not here yet; Mark defines monetary vs fiscal dominance and cites the WWII rate cap and the Treasury-Fed Accord.
corrections.fix: Alan: fiscal dominance (debt so high it dictates monetary policy) is a risk but not yet reached. Mark: under fiscal dominance the central bank is pressured to cap rates and buy debt, as in WWII until the Treasury-Fed Accord.

corrections.issue: Higher EM real yields point was raised by Alan Dunne, not Mark.
corrections.fix: Mark: EM inflation is now below US core inflation (about 3%), making EM relatively more attractive and driving rotation toward EM; Alan adds that EM real yields are therefore higher.
